title: Midnight in the prison
hookLine: at midnight in a dark prison, a child appears with four arms, and his mother asks him to be an ordinary baby
carry: vatsalya: loving God as your own child
tomorrow: how do you carry a newborn across a flooded river?

cards: The Bhagavata sets the scene slowly, as if it doesn't want to rush the night. The sky is clear. The rivers run clean.
Lotuses open on the lakes, birds and bees fill the woods with sound, and a cool, fragrant breeze moves. The sacred fires of the brahmanas burn bright and steady.
And in the middle of the night, in deep darkness, inside a locked cell in Mathura, the text says, the Lord appears from Devaki the way the full moon rises in the east.

teach.b: Vasudeva looks at the newborn, and it is not an ordinary baby. The child has four arms, holding a conch, a mace, a discus and a lotus. A jewel shines at his throat.
He wears yellow silk. Vasudeva knows exactly who this is, and folds his hands in praise. Then Devaki speaks.
Her praise is lovely, and then it turns very practical, very much a mother's.
Please, hide this form. Kamsa must not know you were born here. And this shape is too much for ordinary eyes.
The Lord answers with a secret.

He has been their child before, in two earlier lives, after they spent long years asking for a son like him. Now this is the third time. Think of me as your son, he tells them, and love me, and you will reach me.
Then, while they watch, he does what his mother asked. The four arms, the jewel, the radiance: gone. On the prison floor lies a newborn, like any other.
That is the heart of the birth. The Lord of the universe makes himself small enough to be held. Hindus have a name for loving God this way: vatsalya, a parent's tender love.
At Janmashtami many families stay up until midnight, then bathe a small image of baby Krishna, dress him, and rock him in a tiny cradle.

teach.h: VATSALYA: LOVING GOD AS YOUR CHILD
teach.b: Some homes keep the child Krishna, Bal Gopal, all year: woken, fed and put to bed like one of the family.

how: Hindus celebrate Krishna's birth at Janmashtami. In many homes and temples devotees keep watch until midnight, the hour the Bhagavata gives for the birth, then bathe and dress an image of the infant Krishna and rock him in a small cradle with songs. Some families keep a Bal Gopal (often called Laddu Gopal) at home all year and care for him as a child.

games.q: you're Devaki. your newborn has appeared in divine glory, with four arms, in Kamsa's prison. what do you ask?
o: stay this way and defeat Kamsa now.
hide this form and become an ordinary baby.
leave us and go to heaven.
games.why: she asks him to hide his form, and he does it, becoming an ordinary newborn on the prison floor, small enough to be loved as a child.

practice: Rest your hands in your lap, one cupped inside the other, as if you were holding something small and new. Let your breath slow into that shape.
Devaki asked the Lord to become small enough to hold, and many Hindus picture baby Krishna in their hands just like this. If you pray, hold him there for a minute.
If you don't, hold in mind someone small you love, and keep them there gently.

wordCard.voice: The birth. At midnight in a prison the Lord appears in full glory, and at his mother's request becomes a baby.

orig.note: devaki: Krishna's birth mother, who asks him to become small.

carryVoice: Vatsalya: loving God as your own child. Hold on to that. Tomorrow, a father, a baby and a flooded river. Day eight hundred eighty-one, done.
